definition: The risk that announcing a better future product makes customers stop buying the current one while they wait; named after a 1980s computer maker whose early announcement reportedly froze its sales.
How far ahead of volume availability a vendor publicly dates a product (name plus target year); in this repo measured in months from the first dated mention to planned availability.

An upgraded version of a GPU generation released about a year after the original, such as Blackwell Ultra (B300) after Blackwell or Rubin Ultra after Rubin, usually adding memory and compute on the same architecture.

NVIDIA's rack names give the number of GPUs in one NVLink domain; from CES 2026 the number counts GPU packages rather than dies, so 'Vera Rubin NVL144' became Vera Rubin NVL72 and 'Rubin Ultra NVL576' became Kyber NVL144.
NVIDIA's 2027 GPU generation, announced with four reticle-sized dies, about 100 PFLOPS of FP4 and 1 TB of HBM4E per package for the Kyber rack; reports in 2026 describe a two-die version and 768 GB.

NVIDIA's GPU architecture planned for 2028, shown with a Rosa CPU, an LP40 decode chip, BlueField-5 and ConnectX-10 and a Kyber NVL1152 rack mixing copper and co-packaged optics; specifications not yet published.
